claim: CloudWatch sends events to Amazon EventBridge whenever an alarm is created, updated, deleted or changes alarm state, you can write EventBridge rules that act on them, and CloudWatch guarantees the delivery of alarm state change events to EventBridge.
q: Does CloudWatch send alarm state changes to EventBridge, and is delivery guaranteed?
v: whenever a CloudWatch alarm is created, updated, deleted
guarantees the delivery of alarm state change events
ev: docs/AmazonCloudWatch/latest/monitoring/cloudwatch-and-eventbridge

CloudWatch sends events to Amazon EventBridge whenever a CloudWatch alarm is created, updated, deleted, or changes alarm state. You can use EventBridge and these events to write rules that take actions, such as notifying you, when an alarm changes state.
docs/AmazonCloudWatch/latest/monitoring/cloudwatch-and-eventbridge
CloudWatch guarantees the delivery of alarm state change events to EventBridge.

claim: For a static threshold alarm you choose a CloudWatch metric and a threshold, and the alarm goes to the ALARM state when the metric breaches the threshold for a specified number of evaluation periods.
q: When does a static threshold alarm go to the ALARM state?
v: breaches the threshold for a specified number of evaluation periods
ev: docs/AmazonCloudWatch/latest/monitoring/ConsoleAlarms
The alarm goes to `ALARM` state when the metric breaches the threshold for a specified number of evaluation periods.

claim: CloudWatch Application Signals helps you monitor and improve application performance on AWS and automatically collects data from applications running on services such as Amazon EC2, Amazon ECS and Lambda.
q: Which CloudWatch feature gives application performance monitoring and SLOs?
v: monitor and improve application performance on AWS
automatically collects data from your applications
ev: docs/AmazonCloudWatch/latest/monitoring/CloudWatch-Application-Monitoring-Sections

CloudWatch Application Signals helps you monitor and improve application performance on AWS. It automatically collects data from your applications running on services like Amazon EC2, Amazon ECS, and Lambda.

claim: Container Insights collects, aggregates and summarizes metrics and logs from containerized applications and is available for Amazon ECS, Amazon EKS, Red Hat OpenShift on AWS and Kubernetes platforms on Amazon EC2, including clusters on AWS Fargate.
q: On which container platforms is CloudWatch Container Insights available?
v: Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS), Amazon Elastic Kubernetes Service
ev: docs/AmazonCloudWatch/latest/monitoring/ContainerInsights

Use CloudWatch Container Insights to collect, aggregate, and summarize metrics and logs from your containerized applications and microservices. Container Insights is available for Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS), Amazon Elastic Kubernetes Service (Amazon EKS), RedHat OpenShift on AWS (ROSA), and Kubernetes platforms on Amazon EC2. Container Insights supports collecting metrics from clusters deployed on AWS Fargate for both Amazon ECS and Amazon EKS.

claim: Container Insights collects data as performance log events using the embedded metric format, and when you deploy it, it automatically creates a log group for the performance log events.
q: How does Container Insights store its data?
ev: docs/AmazonCloudWatch/latest/monitoring/ContainerInsights
Container Insights collects data as *performance log events* using [embedded metric format](CloudWatch_Embedded_Metric_Format.md).
docs/AmazonCloudWatch/latest/monitoring/ContainerInsights
When you deploy Container Insights, it automatically creates a log group for the performance log events.

claim: CloudWatch Database Insights is used to monitor and troubleshoot Amazon Aurora and Amazon RDS databases such as RDS for MySQL, RDS for PostgreSQL, RDS for Oracle and RDS for SQL Server, with pre-built dashboards for the database fleet.
q: Which CloudWatch feature monitors the performance of a fleet of RDS and Aurora databases?
v: monitor your database fleet with pre-built, opinionated dashboards
Amazon Aurora MySQL, Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL
ev: docs/AmazonCloudWatch/latest/monitoring/Database-Insights

Use CloudWatch Database Insights to monitor and troubleshoot Amazon Aurora MySQL, Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL, Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL Limitless, Amazon Aurora DSQL, Amazon RDS for SQL Server, RDS for MySQL, RDS for PostgreSQL, RDS for Oracle, RDS for MariaDB, and self-managed PostgreSQL databases at scale.
docs/AmazonCloudWatch/latest/monitoring/Database-Insights
With Database Insights, you can monitor your database fleet with pre-built, opinionated dashboards.

claim: AWS announced that the end-of-life date for Performance Insights was July 31, 2026, and migrated Performance Insights users to CloudWatch Database Insights.
v: end-of-life date for Performance Insights was July 31, 2026
migrated Performance Insights users to Database Insights
ev: docs/AmazonCloudWatch/latest/monitoring/Database-Insights
AWS announced that the end-of-life date for Performance Insights was July 31, 2026, and has migrated Performance Insights users to Database Insights.

claim: Canaries are scripts written in Node.js, Python or Java that create Lambda functions in your account, and they work over both HTTP and HTTPS protocols.
q: What runs a CloudWatch Synthetics canary?
v: They create Lambda functions in your account
over both HTTP and HTTPS protocols
ev: docs/AmazonCloudWatch/latest/monitoring/CloudWatch_Synthetics_Canaries

Canaries are scripts written in Node.js, Python, or Java. They create Lambda functions in your account that use Node.js, Python, or Java as the runtime. Canaries work over both HTTP and HTTPS protocols.

claim: End user data that you collect for CloudWatch RUM is retained for 30 days and then automatically deleted; to keep it longer you can have the app monitor send copies of the telemetry to CloudWatch Logs and adjust the retention of that log group.
q: How long does CloudWatch RUM keep end user data?
v: send copies of the telemetry to CloudWatch Logs
cond: Longer retention needs a copy of the telemetry in CloudWatch Logs.
ev: docs/AmazonCloudWatch/latest/monitoring/CloudWatch-RUM

End user data that you collect for CloudWatch RUM is retained for 30 days and then automatically deleted. If you want to keep the RUM telemetry data for a longer time, you can choose to have the app monitor send copies of the telemetry to CloudWatch Logs in your account.

claim: The cross-account cross-Region CloudWatch console lets you switch between accounts and Regions with selectors to view dashboards, alarms and metrics, and its functionality is integrated with AWS Organizations; AWS recommends cross-account observability for the richest experience within a Region.
q: What does the cross-account cross-Region CloudWatch console let you do?
v: switch between different accounts and Region by using selectors
ev: docs/AmazonCloudWatch/latest/monitoring/Cross-Account-Cross-Region

The cross-account, cross-Region CloudWatch console allows you to easily switch between different accounts and Region by using selectors in the console to view the dashboards, alarms, and metrics in other accounts and Regions.
docs/AmazonCloudWatch/latest/monitoring/Cross-Account-Cross-Region
Cross-account cross-Region console functionality is integrated with AWS Organizations, to help you efficiently build your cross-account cross-Region dashboards.

claim: You can use AWS User Notifications or Amazon SNS to notify users of alarm changes; User Notifications delivers alarm state change events through channels such as email, AWS Chatbot chat and console mobile app push notifications.
q: How can users be notified about CloudWatch alarm changes other than a plain SNS topic?
ev: docs/AmazonCloudWatch/latest/monitoring/Notify_Users_Alarm_Changes
This section explains how you can use AWS User Notifications or Amazon Simple Notification Service to have users be notified of alarm changes.
